records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] email_in_restriction_setting? builds an interpolated Regexp from the raw SiteSetting value, which raises RegexpError when an admin saves a blacklist/whitelist containing regex metacharacters (e.g. '(', '+', '['). A site admin entering a domain list with an unescaped metacharacter in the settings UI makes every User validation crash with RegexpError, breaking all signup and profile saves until the setting is fixed.
records.rationale: In lib/validators/email_validator.rb, email_in_restriction_setting? constructs a Regexp via `regexp = Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true)` where `domains = setting.gsub('.', '\\.')`. Only `.` is escaped; other regex metacharacters in the raw SiteSetting value (e.g. `(`, `[`, `+`) are not escaped and can make the pattern invalid, causing `RegexpError` during validation. Since validate_each calls this for every User email validation when whitelist/blacklist is present, an invalid setting would crash signup/profile saves as described.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] BlockedEmail.should_block? performs a write (match_count increment + save) inside model validation, so any code path that checks validity without persisting still mutates the blocked_emails row. Every User#valid? call with a changed email that matches a blocked record increments match_count and updates last_match_at — stats become meaningless (a user retyping the email in the signup form over multiple attempts inflates counts, and admin previews/valid? checks in console or background jobs record phantom 'matches'), and the validation path now issues an unconditional UPDATE on every signup attempt.
records.rationale: In `lib/validators/email_validator.rb`, validation calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` ("if record.errors[attribute].blank? and BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)"). `BlockedEmail.should_block?` (new model) performs a write: it increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, and `record.save` whenever a matching row exists. Because validations run on `User#valid?` / `save` paths (and can be invoked without persisting the `User`), this diff introduces DB mutation and an UPDATE during the validation step, which can inflate `match_count`/`last_match_at` from repeated validity checks/sign-up

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The blocked-email check is skipped whenever the whitelist/blacklist check already produced an error (`if record.errors[attribute].blank? and BlockedEmail.should_block?`), so match statistics are not collected for emails that are both domain-restricted and blocked. Operators using last_match_at/match_count to triage blocked spammers lose all telemetry for any email that also trips the domain restriction, silently undercounting the exact abuse population the feature was built to track.
records.rationale: In `lib/validators/email_validator.rb`, the blocked-email check is explicitly gated: `if record.errors[attribute].blank? and BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`. Since the whitelist/blacklist logic above can add an error on the same `attribute`, `BlockedEmail.should_block?` (which increments `match_count` and sets `last_match_at`) will not run when a domain restriction error is present. That verifiably prevents match statistics from being collected for emails that trigger both checks.

records.issue_text: [BUG] should_block? increments match_count via read-modify-write (record.match_count += 1; record.save) with no locking or atomic UPDATE, so concurrent validations of the same email lose increments. Two signups with the same blocked email validated concurrently both read match_count=5 and both write 6, permanently undercounting; last_match_at also races. Stats drift silently with no way to detect it; fix is UPDATE blocked_emails SET match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = NOW() WHERE email = ?.
records.rationale: In `app/models/blocked_email.rb` the new `BlockedEmail.should_block?` does `record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save`, and also sets `record.last_match_at = Time.zone.now` before saving. This is a classic read-modify-write without any locking or atomic `UPDATE`, so concurrent validations for the same `email` can overwrite each other’s increments and timestamps (lost update race), permanently undercounting `match_count` and racing `last_match_at`.
records.stripped_text: [BUG] should_block? increments match_count via read-modify-write (record.match_count += 1; record.save) with no locking or atomic UPDATE, so concurrent validations of the same email lose increments. Two signups with the same blocked email validated concurrently both read match_count=5 and both write 6, permanently undercounting; last_match_at also races. Stats drift silently with no way to detect it; fix is UPDATE blocked_emails SET match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = NOW() WHERE email = ?.

This is inherited from the deleted User code, but this diff moves it into a shared validator now applied to every email-validating model, widening the blast radius; a split-on-pipe + escaped alternation would remove the parse risk.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The values.email echoed back to the client comes from user.attributes, which is the model's stored (normalized) email, not the string the user typed, so the client-side rejectedEmails check compares a normalized address against the raw input and never matches when the two differ. When the server normalizes email case (e.g. downcasing before validation), the client pushes the normalized value into rejectedEmails while the user's typed email still differs; the new client-side 'invalid' rejection never fires, the user retries the same address, and gets the server round-trip and generic failure each time — the feature degrades to its pre-diff behavior with no error surfaced.
